fun_fact: Today (Aug 27) is celebrated as World Lakes Day. India's cities were built around lakes — talabs, keres, sarovars and kunds that stored monsoon rain, recharged wells, and cooled the air. As they're encroached and filled in, cities lose their natural flood buffers — which is why places like Bengaluru now swing between floods and water shortages in a warming climate. The good news: lakes can be revived, and citizens are leading the way. [Here's what you could do as a citizen to preserve lakes in your city →](https://citizenmatters.in/bengaluru-lakes-system-functions-sustainability/)
author: Ishwarya and Sailee
